children: Shares of Daktronics rose after the company logged higher profit and sales in its fiscal first quarter, and said it remains on track to achieve its long-term growth targets.
The stock climbed 8.5%, to $21.01, in premarket trading Wednesday. Through Tuesday's close, shares have ebbed 2.4% year to date.

The company, which designs and manufactures video displays and control systems, before the bell posted net income of $19.4 million for its three months ended Aug. 1, up from $16.5 million a year earlier.
Quarterly earnings of 40 cents a share topped analyst expectations for 38 cents a share, according to FactSet.
Sales increased 7.1% to $234.6 million, roughly in line with Wall Street models.

Chief Executive Ramesh Jayaraman said the new fiscal year got off to a strong start, as Daktronics continued to drive momentum, strengthen customer engagement across core markets and build upon a healthy sales pipeline.
He added that the company remains on track to achieve its fiscal 2028 targets.
